name: Whalebone Stays
summary: The rigid bodice of the long eighteenth century. It was linen and silk stiffened with strips of whalebone and laced at the back. It pressed the torso into an upright cone under the gown.

philosophy.core_thesis: A lady stands straight because her stays hold her straight, and the gown above shows the cone that they build.
design_principles: Cut the stays as a cone: wide at the shoulder, narrow at the waist, with a point at the front.
Stiffen the body with whalebone strips 3 to 6 mm wide, set 1 to 2 cm apart in sewn channels.
Join two or three layers of linen with a paste so that the cloth is stiff before any bone goes in.
Set the straps wide and low on the shoulder, so that the shoulders pull back and the chest lifts.
Lace the stays at the back with a spiral cord, and lace a second line at the front if the wearer has no help.
Cover the stays with silk, wool or leather, and bind each edge with a narrow strip of leather.
Wear the stays over a linen chemise, and never let them touch the skin.
anti_patterns: A soft bodice with no bone
A curved, hourglass waist of the later nineteenth century
Machine stitch lines, which are straight and even
A rounded, low bust with a bare back

silhouette.shape: An inverted cone with a flat, upright front, a narrow waist and a point at the lower front.
silhouette.line: A straight, tall line from the shoulder to the point; the back is flat and the shoulders sit far apart.
silhouette.fit: Hard and close on the ribs, with the weight of the garment on the hip bone, not on the shoulder.
silhouette.proportion: Length 38 to 45 cm at the front; waist 55 to 65 cm for a young woman; tabs below the waist 8 to 12 cm.
rules: Keep the front flat from the neck to the point, with no curve at the stomach.
Cut the neck low and square, so that the chemise shows at the edge.
Cut the back narrow and pull it together with lacing.
Cut tabs below the waist so that the stays lie flat over the hip.
Leave a gap at the front for a decorated stomacher.

fabrics.rule: Make the body from two or three layers of strong linen, stiffen it with whalebone, and cover it with silk, wool or leather.

methods: spiral cord lace at the back
construction.closures: A cord laces through two rows of hand-sewn eyelets at the back; some stays also lace at the front.
construction.details: Shoulder straps that tie or pin at the front, and an open front for a stomacher. A busk pocket and a bound edge of kidskin or ribbon.

surface.pattern: Plain linen for the working woman; for the court, silk with small floral embroidery or a woven pattern.
surface.gloss: Linen and wool at 2–6 GU; silk satin and damask at 20–45 GU.
surface.wear: A used pair of stays takes the shape of one body; the bone bends, the linen darkens at the waist, and the eyelets show wear.

palette.strategy: Natural linen and undyed bone inside the gown; a single pale or deep colour of silk for stays that show.

processes: cut by a master stay-maker, who was a man
paste and quilt of the linen layers
cut and shave of the whalebone strips
eyelets sewn by hand with silk thread
making.scale: Made to measure by a trade of stay-makers; each pair took several days to make and fitted one body.
making.signs: Hand-sewn channels with small, even stitches, a bone in each channel, hand-bound eyelets, and a flat front with a point.

pieces.form: Full-boned stays with tabs, laced at the back, covered in silk
Working-class stays in plain linen with a leather binding
Court stays with an open front for a stomacher, in a woven silk
Linen chemise worn under the stays
Knitted silk stockings tied below the knee

canonical_works.maker: Denis Diderot and Jean le Rond d'Alembert

lineage.root: The pair of stays is a root of the underwear branch. The boned bodice of the sixteenth century is the older form, and no earlier style of the branch is in the data.

emotion.target_response: A feeling of order and discipline: an upright body, a firm line and the quiet skill of the stay-maker.

use_cases: a costume brief for a period film
a museum label or object study
a historical reconstruction of court dress
avoid_when: the brief wants a modern or Victorian hourglass corset
the brief wants elastic or comfort
the brief is a nineteenth-century lingerie look

modifiers.how: Cut the waist smaller, curve the hip, and add a steel busk and metal eyelets; keep the bone.
Add the wide hoop and the silk gown, and keep the stays flat and conical under them.

ornament_level.note: Working stays are plain; court stays carry silk embroidery.
